summary: Heidi Fjeld is a scholar in Tibetology who earned her Doctor Rerum Politicarum at the University of Oslo (~2001–2006) under Signe Howell. She served as a postdoctoral fellow at the University of Oslo from around 2007 to 2010.

Heidi I. Koppl specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She completed an MA at the University of Copenhagen under Christian K. Wedemeyer and also studied under the traditional teacher Khenpo Sherab Zangpo.

Heidi Pauwels is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. She studied at KU Leuven in 1983 and 1986, earned her PhD at the University of Washington in 1994, and held a post at the University of Washington around 1996.

Heinrich Blochmann (1838–1878) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He pursued studies at Leipzig University from around 1855 to 1857 and at the University of Calcutta from around 1860 to 1861.

Heinrich Ewald (1803–1875) worked in linguistics, religious studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Göttingen under Johann Gottfried Eichhorn, and held professorships at Göttingen (1824–1837, 1848–1867) and the University of Tübingen (1838–1848).

Heinrich Hettrich (1947–2020) was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at the University of Giessen and Saarland University, and held posts at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1982–1988), Saarland University (~1988–1989), and the University of Würzburg (~1989–2012).

Heinrich Hübschmann (1848–1908) was a scholar of linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. He studied at the University of Jena (~1868–1872) and under Martin Haug (~1871–1872), later holding a post at Leipzig University (~1876–1877).

Heinrich Kiepert (1818–1899) was a scholar in history and archaeology who studied at Frederick William University Berlin in 1837. He held positions at the Landes-Industrie-Comptoir zu Weimar (1845–1852) and at Frederick William University Berlin in 1859.

Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer (1801–1888) was a linguist who founded the Deutsche Morgenländische Gesellschaft. He completed his studies at Leipzig University (~1819–1824) and subsequently held a post there from around 1835 until 1888.

Heinrich Lüders (1869–1943) was an Indologist, linguist, and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn. He held posts at Göttingen, Rostock, Kiel, and became Ordinarius für indische Philologie at Berlin in 1909.

Heinrich Schweizer-Sidler (1815–1894) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied under Bernhard Hirzel from around 1835 to 1838 and held an academic post at the University of Zurich from around 1841 to 1894.
Heinrich Uhle (1842–1925) was an Indology scholar who studied under Hermann Brockhaus from around 1860 to 1865. He later served as a professor at the Kreuzschule from around 1874 to 1907.

Heinrich Wenzel (1855–1893) worked in Indology and Tibetology. He studied at Jena, Tübingen, Leipzig, and under Heinrich August Jäschke, Léon Feer, and Georg von der Gabelentz, later completing his Habilitation at Leipzig University in 1887.

Heinrich Zimmer (1851–1910) was a linguist and Indologist who studied in Strasbourg and Berlin under Roth, Goldschmidt, Weber, Scherer, and Windisch. He held posts at Greifswald (~1881–1901), Berlin (~1901–1910), Heidelberg University, and Columbia University.

Heinz Bechert (1932–2005) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Saarland University (~1956–1964), served as Director at the University of Göttingen (~1965–2000), and was a series editor at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences (~1973–2005).

Heinz Mode (1913–1992) worked in archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under George Peiris Malalasekera, Otto Fischer, and completed a doctorate at the University of Basel, later serving as Professor of Oriental Archaeology at Halle-Wittenberg (~1948–1978).

Helen Hardacre is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. Her career includes serving as a faculty member in the Department of Religion at Princeton University (attested 1988–1996) and holding a post at Harvard University around 1990.

Helen J. Baroni specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied at Grinnell College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Columbia University under Paul B. Watt, and she took up a post at the University of Hawaii around 1993.
Helena Blankleder is a scholar in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under the traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, both attested in 1999.
Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from around 1979 to 1984. She held an academic post at Rice University around 1990.
